title: linux: safely resize a partition that is nearly full
scenario: On linux, a hard operational problem: Ridimensiona una partizione quasi piena per un volume adiacente con spazio libero, senza perdita dati. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: safely resize a partition that is nearly full

initial_state: # fixture: linux host prepared for 'safely resize a partition that is nearly full'
expected_reasoning: Partition resizing is destructive if mis-ordered — back up / snapshot first.
Resize in the correct order (unmount/quiesce, resize partition, then filesystem, or grow-online where supported).
Verify the new size and integrity before returning to service.
expected_commands: # linux-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: safely resize a partition that is nearly full
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'safely resize a partition that is nearly full' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: safely resize a partition that is nearly full

possible_mistakes: Resize the filesystem before/after the partition in the wrong order.
Skip the backup on a destructive op.
hints: Order matters: shrink FS before partition, grow partition before FS.
alternative_solution: Use LVM/APFS elasticity to avoid a raw partition resize entirely.
edge_cases: Grow-online works for some FS; others need the volume offline.
goal: Ridimensiona una partizione quasi piena per un volume adiacente con spazio libero, senza perdita dati.
